entries.capability: Music generation with realistic vocals (final production)
entries.model: MiniMax Music 3 (DiT fp16 4.6 GB / int8 2.3 GB low-VRAM + text encoder pruned int8 8.6 GB + VAE DAW 0.2 GB)
entries.time_measured: ~1-2 min per song (RTX 5090, 30 steps cfg 1.7); up to 360 s in length (model hard limit)
entries.quality_notes: Very realistic vocals (timbre, falsetto, effects) and clean mixing; long-duration structural coherence and exact lyric fidelity are its strong points. Native 32 kHz audio. 3-section prose caption (Global Metadata / Vocal Details / Arrangement); structure tags only in lyrics. Proven VRAM rule: songs >~120 s require --tiled-decode (without it, fp32 VAE decode exhausts the 5090's 32 GB and the system swaps). Goes through the GPU broker: during the swap the agent's LLM stops (concurrent work paused) → always launch in background with a warning to the user.
entries.when_not_to_use: Fast iteration, section editing, reference audio or LoRA (ACE Step 1.5 XL wins there); not suited for heavy general audio per A/B (Aug 2026 the user preferred ACE); >360 s; the license excludes local deployment in EU/US/UK/KR.
entries.license: MiniMax-Music3 Community License (excludes local deployment in EU/US/UK/KR)
entries.source_model_repo: MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-Music3 (reempacado oficial: Comfy-Org/MiniMax-Music-3; nodos nativos ComfyUI >= 0.33)

entries.capability: Fast, iterable music generation (with editing and LoRA)
entries.model: ACE Step 1.5 XL Turbo (decoder 4B + text encoder 4B, 8 steps CFG 1.0; variantes xl-merge SFT, 2B high, AIO standard)
entries.time_measured: ~6 s per song with turbo (RTX 5090, comparison in the minimax-music3 skill); disk per model: not measured
entries.quality_notes: The best local generator for general audio quality and heavy genres per community consensus (Aug 2026). Edit mode with partial denoise (must repeat the original --tags/--lyrics/--bpm/--key), reference audio for timbre/style and personalization LoRA. Explicit flags --bpm/--key/--language. Output MP3 320 kbps or FLAC. Max duration ~300 s. Comma-separated tags with no metadata inside. Goes through the GPU broker (pauses the LLM during the swap).
entries.when_not_to_use: Ultra-realistic vocals or >5 min structure with literal lyric fidelity (MiniMax Music 3 stands out there); editing without the original conditioning (incoherent results).
entries.license: Apache 2.0 (per the comparison in the minimax-music3 skill)

entries.capability: Text-to-speech with voice cloning (voice clone, speaker preset, voice design)
entries.model: Qwen3-TTS 12Hz 1.7B (por defecto) / 0.6B (--fast, ~3x más rápido en CPU)
entries.time_measured: no wall-time measurement per clip (broker timeout 900 s by default); 0.6B ~3x faster than 1.7B; CPU fallback if VRAM is short
entries.quality_notes: Multilingual (ES/EN/ZH and more). Cloning with --ref-audio + --ref-text (5-15 s of reference); predefined speaker mode with --instruct; voice design mode with a natural-language description. Output WAV 24 kHz mono. Known issue: it clips the last syllable → add 0.3 s of silence with ffmpeg apad (tested on 45+ clips) and verify the audio with Whisper (≥80% of keywords, language ≥0.9). Clips <20 s; split long text (never summarize). ETHICS: clone voices only from your own voice or with the person's explicit consent; label all AI-generated content. Goes through the GPU broker (gpu-exec: stops the LLM, generates, relaunches it).
entries.when_not_to_use: Long texts in a single pass (each chunk pays the broker handover); do not use the llama-server API for TTS (it serves the chat model, not a TTS); real-time voice for home automation (that's where the Edge TTS bridge goes).

entries.capability: Voice identity cloning in generated video (voice + video + lip-sync together)
entries.model: ID-LoRA para LTX-2.3 (checkpoint ~1.1 GB; también clon por audio de referencia en H3/LTX: hasta 3 clips de 2-15 s, 15 s total)
entries.time_measured: not measured (wall-time per video clip not listed in the files)
entries.quality_notes: A ~5 s reference clip fixes the voice identity (timbre, pitch, cadence) and persists across clips; the model generates synchronized video and audio without a separate TTS step. Reference audio ~5 s = fingerprint, not playback. Prompt with [VISUAL]/[SPEECH]/[SOUNDS] sections; [SPEECH] ≤~10 s (more than 15 s truncates). Pretrained per-speaker checkpoints (CelebVHQ 872 speakers / TalkVid 1,973). ID-LoRA nodes require ComfyUI with PR #13111+ (HTTP 500 = unrecognized node). ETHICS: only your own voice or with explicit consent; label AI content; do not impersonate identities.
entries.when_not_to_use: Pure audio TTS (use Qwen3-TTS); dialogue >15 s per clip; older ComfyUI without the nodes; third-party voices without consent.

entries.capability: Local audio transcription (STT) with OpenAI-compatible API
entries.model: faster-whisper medium int8 en CPU (por defecto; soporta tiny/base/small/medium/large-v3)
entries.time_measured: ~10 s per ≤20 s clip on CPU (TTS verification flow, faster-whisper medium int8); global RTF not measured — the server returns duration and processing_time per request to compute it
entries.quality_notes: Dependency-free stdlib HTTP server: POST /v1/audio/transcriptions (multipart, OpenAI-compatible) and /transcribe (raw body), /health. Lazy model (loads on the first request; --preload optional). medium int8 uses ~5 GB of CPU RAM (does not touch the GPU). Integrates with the broker (monitors :8787 and relaunches it if it falls over). Example endpoint: http://<YOUR_SERVER>:8787/v1/audio/transcriptions.
entries.when_not_to_use: No RTF measured for long real-time audio; for minimum latency, upsizing the model requires measuring; not a multi-user production server.

entries.capability: Voice for home assistant (Home Assistant Assist) via the Wyoming protocol
entries.model: wyoming-whisper-bridge (STT) + wyoming-edge-tts-bridge (TTS, Microsoft Edge TTS, voz es-ES-AlvaroNeural)
entries.quality_notes: Lightweight bridges that translate the Wyoming protocol (Home Assistant) to already-running services: the STT bridge reuses the local whisper-server (:8787) instead of loading a second model — listens 16 kHz/16-bit/mono, emits Transcript on AudioStop; default port 10300. The TTS bridge uses Edge TTS (Microsoft's cloud service, free, no local model) and converts MP3→PCM with ffmpeg; default port 10200. Examples: ws://<YOUR_SERVER>:10300 (STT), ws://<YOUR_SERVER>:10200 (TTS).
entries.when_not_to_use: Edge TTS does NOT work without internet (it is not local) — for 100% local TTS use Qwen3-TTS or Piper-style outside this stack; not for transcribing large files (use the whisper-server directly).

entries.capability: Shared GPU gateway: single-queue broker that serializes the GPU jobs of all agents
entries.model: comfyui-broker.py (referencia de implementación; patrón genérico utilizable por cualquier agente)
entries.time_measured: batch_wait_seconds=5 by default (window that groups nearby jobs into a single session); full handover profile→engine started ~28 s → health loaded ~64 s; per-job timeouts 900-1800 s
entries.quality_notes: GENERIC PATTERN: a single HTTP process acts as a serial queue for a GPU that cannot be shared. Cycle: (1) saves the llama-server's KV slots (GET /slots + action=save), (2) kills llama-server to free VRAM, (3) starts ComfyUI and runs the API-graph (with placeholder 'replacements' and 'copies'), (4) stops ComfyUI, (5) relaunches and warms up llama-server and (6) restores the KV slots — the agent continues with its context intact. Endpoints: POST /v1/generate (workflow JSON or workflow_path) and POST /v1/gpu-exec (any command with GPU access; async:true returns job_id; it also serves files as base64 via stdout). Default ports configurable via env: broker 8791, ComfyUI 8000, llama-server 30000, whisper 8787 (it monitors and relaunches it). The broker is intentionally declared generic: it accepts ready-made ComfyUI API JSON. GATEWAY RULE: GPU jobs are serialized in this queue; during the swap the LLM serving the conversation is paused (the agent's turn may die and resume once the engine is restored) → ALWAYS launch in background with notify, warn the user of the few-minute outage, and do not run two expert-streaming engines in parallel (they fight over VRAM/RAM). Extra model path via the model-paths yaml.
entries.when_not_to_use: Not needed if the LLM and the diffusion models fit in VRAM simultaneously, or if only one consumer uses the GPU; not a multi-GPU balancer and it does not serve synchronous chat inference.
entries.workflow_ref: scripts/comfyui-broker.py; scripts/start-comfyui-broker-window.ps1; scripts/comfyui-extra-model-paths.yaml; skills/strata-profile-switch/SKILL.md (handover via broker)
entries.source_model_repo: null (script propio; depende de ggml-org/llama.cpp y Comfy-Org/ComfyUI)

entries.capability: Local LLM on GPU — serving and tuning llama.cpp (GGUF) for agents
entries.model: llama-server (ggml-org/llama.cpp) con Qwen 27B denso como banco (UD-Q6_K, NVFP4+MTP)
entries.disk_gb: 14-54 (27B según cuantización: IQ4_XS ~14, Q4_K_M ~15, Q5_K_M ~18, Q6_K ~27, Q8_0 ~54 GB)
entries.time_measured: RTX 5090 32GB: Qwen3.6-27B NVFP4+MTP 74.4→90.8 t/s (+22% from MTP); 27B Q6_K dense (retired) ~100-106 t/s decode and prefill ~2067 t/s; 8-9B llama.cpp 134-213 t/s decode vs vLLM 83-89 (single-user; with 4 users vLLM 341 vs 123); Mac class (M4 Pro, MLX, Qwen3.5-27B Q4 with MTP): 15.3→23.3 t/s
entries.quality_notes: Quantization guide: chat Q4_K_M; code/technical Q5_K_M or Q6_K; Q8 only if it fits; AWQ-INT4 does NOT load in llama.cpp (pre-processing only); DeltaNet hybrid models (Qwen 27B) are the most quant-sensitive — keeping attention/DeltaNet in Q8_0 (NVFP4 only in MLP) matters more than squeezing the FFN; 6-bit QAT does not beat an imatrix PTQ. Context measured on the 5090: 100-120K with the recommended config (Q5_K_M + DFlash + KV turbo4/turbo3_tcq, ~26-28 GB VRAM) and up to 262144 with --cache-ram 32768 + checkpoints; quality baseline at 200K: 25/25 probes (needle+multi-hop+distractors) with KV K Q8_0/V q5_1. Speculation: merged MTP (--spec-type draft-mtp), distribution-identical; n-max 2→3 gave +7.3% TG only with acceptance ≥65%; DFlash wins on plain text but collapses on long outputs (47→30 t/s) and has an open bug with mmproj (#27408: ~1.8% acceptance, 27-43 t/s with images). Multimodal: mmproj-*.gguf is a SEPARATE projector, not the main model; --no-mmproj-offload leaves it on CPU and frees ~2-3 GB of VRAM for KV; native video via input_video (build with MTMD_VIDEO; 4.5 s clip → 10.8K prompt tokens, ~12 s response; on Windows it needs an anti-deadlock wrapper due to bug #24429). reasoning_effort lives in the chat-template (llama-server --chat-template-kwargs; Ollama destroys it). Golden rules: the server log is the truth (/props lies about MTP); bucket t/s by context band; benchmark only with an idle server.
entries.when_not_to_use: Large MoE exceeding RAM/VRAM on a 64 GB machine → Strata-style streaming engine; multi-user/API serving → vLLM; vLLM modelopt/compressed-tensors checkpoints do not load in GGUF (even if the repo is named 'X-NVFP4').
entries.source_model_repo: ggml-org/llama.cpp; bancos citados: unsloth (UD-Q6_K), LibertAIDAI/Qwen3.6-27B-NVFP4-MTP-GGUF, z-lab/Qwen3.6-27B-DFlash

entries.capability: Local LLM at the edge: cheap auxiliary server (Raspberry Pi 5 / mini PC) for asynchronous tasks
entries.model: Qwen3.5-4B-MTP GGUF Q4_K_M (2.78 GB, MTP nativo) en llama.cpp compilado con BLIS
entries.time_measured: Pi 5 (7.9 GB RAM): prompt-processing 13.75 t/s @4K and 12.35 t/s @6K with BLIS (+42-43% vs OpenBLAS), 7.15 t/s @20K; generation 3.2-7.2 t/s with MTP+ngram (classification ~5-6 t/s); 40K context (review pass) = 40-50 min — keep those tasks on the GPU
entries.quality_notes: Offloads the main GPU (frees cache-ram) and removes cloud calls for short asynchronous tasks (titles, triage, short summaries). BLIS on ARM64 with manual paths (no .pc in Debian). KV K q5_1 + V q4_0 (~18 B/token) → 96K practical context on 7.9 GB (128K causes swap-thrashing). Validated flags: -t 4 -tb 4 -c 98304 --cache-type-k q5_1 --cache-type-v q4_0 --ubatch-size 2048 --spec-type draft-mtp,ngram-simple --spec-draft-n-max 3 --reasoning off; example port <YOUR_SERVER>:8082 (OpenAI-compatible). Verify MTP: 'draft acceptance' 0.85-0.95 in the log. Honest note: no 27B is served on the Pi — the 27B measured on small hardware is MLX on M4 Pro (23.3 t/s); the Pi runs 4B.
entries.when_not_to_use: Latency-sensitive tasks, context >20K tokens or outputs >200 tokens in real time (30-40 s per long generation); Qwen3.5 thinks by default (--reasoning off mandatory).
entries.license: MIT (llama.cpp; model license not stated in the files)

entries.capability: Large local MoE LLM on a 64 GB RAM box — NVFP4 engine with experts cached across VRAM+RAM+SSD
entries.model: Strata NVFP4 (fork sergqwer/strata-nvfp4 de Niko1221/Strata) con pack qwen-nvfp4-gptq de Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (MoE 125B-A6B)
entries.time_measured: RTX 5090 + 64 GB DDR5 + 8 cores: warm decode 90-102 t/s (short ctx, full page-locked residency with --ram-budget 42-46); per-band medians 67-92 t/s between 32K and ≥140K; cold prefill 714/1406/3000 t/s @1K/4K/16K and ~4470-4979 t/s incremental; prefix reuse 99%+ at 126K; 135-165 K session restored from disk in ~1.7 s (~2000 MB/s); broker→new-profile handover: engine started ~28 s, health OK ~64 s
entries.quality_notes: Only a cache lives in VRAM (the weights do not); ~42 GiB of experts page-locked in RAM and the rest on SSD. Served context 262144 with int8 KV (Walsh-Hadamard rotation, 0.265% error). The demonstrated bottleneck on this box is the CPU cores (7 expert workers + host on 8 cores), not VRAM or PCIe. Dual normal/uncensor profiles via vector control mounted as two startup configs over the same pack (KV does not cross profiles: the first turn after switching pays a full re-read, measured 17.8 s for 70K). Engine/profile changes ALWAYS through the broker (a single active engine). Measured intelligence (GSM8K+HellaSwag+HumanEval subset, T1.0/0.95/20, xhigh): pooled 92.45% (2026-10-18). Ledger rule: bucket by context band, do not cross packs in one comparison.
entries.when_not_to_use: Windows with <96 GB may not need this path if a dense model fits in VRAM; NVIDIA's FP4-Local pack: its license prohibits vector control (no uncensor); similar engines require >110 GB of host; do not start two expert engines in parallel with llama-server/Strata.
entries.license: null (gptq pack: not stated; nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP4-Local: NVIDIA Open Model License — prohibits vector control)
entries.source_model_repo: sergqwer/strata-nvfp4 (fork de Niko1221/Strata); pack bundle qwen-nvfp4-gptq; modelo base Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

entries.capability: Benchmarking local LLMs: speed and intelligence with honest methodology
entries.model: llama-benchy (HTTP, pp/tg) + suite de inteligencia GSM8K/ARC/HellaSwag/PIQA/HumanEval/PPL + McNemar
entries.time_measured: HumanEval (164 cases × 2000+ tokens) ~40+ min; GSM8K+HellaSwag+HumanEval subset ~65 min/pass (Flash-Next T1.0; orca ~150 min for HumanEval); full v2 suite ~4.2 h; v1 suite 27B xhigh 44.5 min; speed under xhigh load ~61-65 t/s vs ~98-101 t/s idle
entries.quality_notes: Verified methodology: always the real --tokenizer (the gpt2 fallback fakes counts); --runs 1 for honesty (the ngram cache inflates runs 2-3 by up to 3-5×: 135→243→716 t/s same prompt); the server log (slot print_timing) is the truth — /props says 'none' with MTP active and probes against a live slot come out 10-15% low; bucket t/s by context band; PPL is NOT intelligence (real case: PPL 1.2470 with reasoning at 11%); max_tokens ≥8192 with xhigh (2000 cuts the thinking → 0%); check finish_reason (length invalidates the probe); statistical power: only HumanEval (n=164, SE 1.7pp) resolves 2-4pp deltas → use McNemar on discordant items; saturated ARC-Easy/PIQA (100) do not discriminate; audit the datasets' expected values before comparing. Real suite data (27B RTX 5090): Qwen3.8 UD-Q6_K GSM8K 88.2 / HumanEval 92.7 (2026-08-14); NVFP4 1f+MTP avg 90.4 / HumanEval 86.0; full quant table in the skill.
entries.when_not_to_use: Do not compare columns from different suites (v1 greedy vs v2 T1.0) or cross packs/engines in one comparison; do not use this suite for throughput (that is llama-benchy/benchy + log); PPL not comparable across models with this measurement (1 token/chunk).
